integration_note: MERGE BLOCKERS (code, not facts). None of the three fields (conditional_admission, min_gpa_percent, language_waiver) exists in src/lib/proposals/merge.ts PROGRAM_FACT_FIELDS, in data/schemas/programs.schema.json, or anywhere in src/, so scripts/merge-proposals.ts will SKIP every accepted row as 'unknown program field'. A maintainer must add the fields to the Program type, the schema, merge.ts and the renderer before these rows can land. Shape notes: conditional_admission and min_gpa_percent use the gpa_rule shape {scale, min, text}, but uccs-mscs.conditional_admission has min null and value_gpa_rule requires a number, so the new schema must allow a null min or treat the field as text-first. language_waiver is a plain string and overlaps language_req.waiver; Wuerzburg's value equals its existing waiver text. UI: every accepted conditional_admission is discretionary (provisional, director's discretion, or 'can be invited' to an aptitude test). Show it as 'may be considered', never as an eligibility pass, and show NYIT's two-semester limit and UCCS's GRE Q 148 requirement for international applicants next to it. All source hosts are already on data/ingest.allowlist.json.

value.text: GPA below 3.0: if admitted at all, expect provisional admission. GPA below 2.75: if admitted, the Graduate School requires provisional admission. No lower floor is stated.

proposals.evidence_snippet: Students with an average GPA below 3.0, if admitted at all, should expect to be admitted provisionally. If a student with a GPA below 2.75 is admitted, then the Graduate School requires provisional admission.
proposals.notes: Same paragraph also says: 'Students with an average below 3.0 but above 2.75 will be considered on an individual basis' and 'Students who recently earned an undergraduate degree with a GPA below 3.00 will be required to take the GRE (Graduate Record Examination) before they can be considered for admission. A score of 148 (new grading scale) on the quantitative portion is considered favorable.' So a 2.5/4 applicant needs the GRE and, if admitted, is admitted provisionally. The page does not say what provisional status requires after enrolment. Not a promise of admission.

review.checks: verify-snippet --file: 18/18 FOUND on the first run, no network errors. peek-page re-read eas.uccs.edu live on 2026-11-24. This is UCCS's official MS Computer Science page (College of Engineering and Applied Science). The regular minimum is printed in the same paragraph: 'The student should have an undergraduate grade point average of at least 3.0 on a scale of 4.0' (so cgpa_4 is stated, not assumed). The next sentences say 'Students with an average GPA below 3.0, if admitted at all, should expect to be admitted provisionally. If a student with a GPA below 2.75 is admitted, then the Graduate School requires provisional admission.' The value matches this exactly. Provisional admission is a real route below the 3.0 regular minimum. min null is correct because the page prints no lower floor. The rule covers all applicants. The paragraph also points international applicants to extra requirements: the International Students section on the same page makes 'All sections of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE)' required 'with at least 148 on the quantitative portion' unless the applicant has a U.S. ABET CS degree with a 3.0 GPA. That is stricter than the 'considered favorable' wording quoted in notes, so a Pakistani applicant below 3.0 must plan on GRE Q 148 or more. A NACES/AICE course-by-course evaluation is required, so the GPA UCCS judges may be the evaluated GPA rather than the raw CGPA. The page does not say whether provisional admission comes with an I-20, and the value does not claim it does. This is not a promise of admission.

value.text: Undergraduate GPA 2.5 to 2.84: at the director's discretion, may be given the chance to qualify for full matriculation by earning a GPA of 3.0 or higher in the first four graduate courses. May also have to take parts of the GRE.

proposals.evidence_snippet: Applicants who do not qualify for full matriculation and have an undergraduate GPA between 2.5 and 2.84 may, at the discretion of the director, be given the opportunity to demonstrate qualifications for full matriculation by achieving a GPA of 3.0 or higher in the first four graduate courses.
proposals.notes: Source is the official New York Tech Catalog 2026-2027 (catalog.nyit.edu). Same catalog entry continues: 'such students may be required to take one or more parts of the GRE' and 'students in this category will not be permitted to continue in the program for more than two semesters unless they have qualified for fully matriculated status'. It also says 'Students of foreign universities with a CGPA of 2.7 (on a 4.0 scale) would automatically be denied a GRE waiver', so a Pakistani 2.5 applicant should plan on the GRE. The program admission page (https://www.nyit.edu/academics/degrees/computer-science-ms/admission-requirements/) words it as: 'Minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.85 for full matriculation. If you do not satisfy this criterion, you may be admitted at the dean's discretion.' Discretionary, not guaranteed. GPA may be judged on a NACES credential evaluation rather than the raw Pakistani CGPA.

review.checks: verify-snippet --file: 18/18 FOUND on the first run, no network errors. peek-page re-read catalog.nyit.edu live. This is the official New York Tech Catalog 2026-2027, Computer Science M.S. The regular minimum is printed first: 'Minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.85 for full matriculation'. The snippet follows it, then: 'In addition, such students may be required to take one or more parts of the GRE and meet individual departmental requirements. In general, students in this category will not be permitted to continue in the program for more than two semesters unless they have qualified for fully matriculated status, or there are special extenuating circumstances.' The value (GPA 2.5 to 2.84, director's discretion, 3.0 or higher in the first four graduate courses, possible GRE parts) is an exact reading. min 2.5 is the lower bound of that range. The paragraph names no scale, but the same page's GRE section uses '(on a 4.0 scale)', so cgpa_4 is consistent. I also re-read the program page (nyit.edu/academics/degrees/computer-science-ms/admission-requirements/). It agrees: 'If you do not satisfy this criterion, you may be admitted at the dean's discretion.' (That page says dean; the catalog says director.) Both pages say foreign-university CGPA below 3.0 must take the GRE, and a 2.7 CGPA is 'automatically' denied a GRE waiver except in extenuating circumstances. The route is discretionary. The two-semester limit is a real condition and the UI should show it next to the value.

Grade of Bachelor's degree Required grade in the aptitude test Required grade if Bachelor's degree in standard length of programme 2.6 - 3.0 4.0 No aptitude test required 3.1 - 3.5 3.0 3.5 3.6 - 4.0 2.0 2.5

Same page: 'If you fulfil these requirements but with a grade worse than 2.5 you can be invited to an oral aptitude test for admittance' (30-minute oral test on theoretical, practical and technical computer science; may switch to a written exam if many tests are needed). review.checks: verify-snippet --file: 18/18 FOUND on the first run, no network errors. peek-page re-read informatik.uni-wuerzburg.de live. This is the official JMU Wuerzburg Institute of Computer Science application page for the MSc Computer Science. It says: 'If you fulfil the admission requirements and your degree grade is 2.5 or better (in the German grading system) you can be directly admitted to the programme. If you fulfil these requirements but with a grade worse than 2.5 you can be invited to an oral aptitude test for admittance.' The table read live is: 2.6-3.0 needs 4.0, or 'No aptitude test required' if the degree took the standard length; 3.1-3.5 needs 3.0 (3.5); 3.6-4.0 needs 2.0 (2.5). That matches the value exactly. This is a real route below the 2.5 direct-admission grade. scale german with min 4.0 follows the src/lib/types.ts rule (min is the worst acceptable grade on a lower-is-better scale) and equals the table's last row. The page also says the test is a 30-minute oral exam (theoretical, practical and technical CS) that may switch to a written exam. It applies to international applicants: the same page lists their documents, including the uni-assist VPD. 'Can be invited' is not a guarantee. The other requirements still apply (180 ECTS, 100 ECTS in CS and maths including 25 in theory, a 10-ECTS CS thesis, and the language requirement). The page does not give a Pakistani CGPA to German grade conversion.

rejected.reason: The snippet is verbatim, but the program check fails. The limited-status rule is a campus-wide Graduate College rule that applies only 'with support from the academic program'. I re-read the Siebel School's own admissions page (siebelschool.illinois.edu/admissions/graduate/applications-process-requirements) live. It frames the 3.0 as a hard bar: 'The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign policy requires applicants to hold at least a 3.0/4.0 or higher GPA in the last two years of their undergraduate study to be eligible for graduate studies on this campus.' The MS program page publishes no limited-status route for GPA. Putting a 'conditional admission' route on the MS CS page would claim a route the department does not offer in public. The Graduate College country page (grad.illinois.edu/admissions/country) renders by JavaScript, so its Pakistan minimum was not readable. A human could email Siebel admissions and ask whether they support limited status below 3.0.

Wrong program. I re-read the page live: the answer sits under 'Pathway Programs FAQs > Admission FAQs'. That section is about admission 'into this program', the 15-credit self-supporting Pathway to Computing graduate certificate ($640 per credit hour). It is not the MSCS. The page says the certificate gives 'priority admission into the MSCS program' and its credits 'do not count toward the master's programs'. Nothing on the page applies the case-by-case GPA exceptions to direct MSCS applicants or to international (F-1) applicants. The proposer's own reviewer note says the same. This should not be shown as an MSCS admission route.

This is not a conditional admission route into this program. I re-read the page live: 'If you do not meet our minimum requirements you may still be able to apply for one of our pre-master's courses.' That is admission to a separate course. The page does not name which pre-master's course leads to the MSc Advanced Computer Science, and it gives no progression mark. The value also infers the scale. The page prints 'Pass grade (for a pre-master's course) 40% or GPA 1.0' with no scale, and the proposal stores it as cgpa_4 min 1.0. If the pre-master's matters, it belongs in a separate pathway or program record with its own progression rule, not here as a 1.0 GPA floor for this MSc.

Wrong level: this is a university floor, not the program minimum. I re-read imperial.ac.uk accepted-qualifications live. The Pakistan entry is the minimum 'To be considered for admission to postgraduate study' (a 4-year HEC-funded bachelor's from 2016 on, 75% or better, 'Selectors may demand a higher mark'). The MSc Computing course page, also re-read live, says outright: 'please note that the standards listed are the minimum for entry to Imperial, and not specifically this Department.' The course's own minimum is 'A First-Class degree in a subject without substantial computing content'. Imperial publishes no Pakistani percentage for a First. Storing min 75 as this program's min_gpa_percent would tell a 75% student they meet the minimum when they may not. The course is also a conversion course, outside the target group for BS CS graduates.

The proposal is marked basis 'inferred' and combines two pages, which fails the no-inference check. The snippet (SGS equivalency table, re-read live: 'Pakistan Mid-B GPA 2.80 or 67.5% A Minus GPA 3.40 or 75% B Plus GPA 3.10 or 70.75%') holds no MScAC requirement. The B+ requirement is on a different page (mscac.utoronto.ca/apply, re-read live: 'A standing equivalent to at least B+ (U of T 77-79%) in their final year (i.e., two terms)'). The requirement also covers final-year standing only. A program-level min_gpa_percent of 70.75 would be compared with a student's cumulative percentage, which is the wrong measure. Both pieces are correct on their own pages. A human can add them as a final-year min_gpa_rule with an explicit 'final year (two terms)' basis, or record the SGS row as a conversion rule.

The value's 'Waiver only if the student has completed a degree in the US' goes further than the official sources support. The program page does say 'If the student has completed a degree in the US, this requirement may be waived.' But the UCCS Graduate School's English Proficiency Requirements page (graduateschool.uccs.edu/english-proficiency-requirements, re-read live; linked from uccs.edu international graduate details) lists 'You have received or will receive a post-secondary degree where English is the language (medium) of instruction' as one of the methods 'Academic programs use', with an official MOI letter if the transcript does not say so. It tells applicants: 'Please contact your program to verify which method(s) they allow.' Its program chart lists only test scores for Computer Science MS & PhD (TOEFL 80 / 4.5, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115), not which waiver methods CS accepts. Whether CS accepts an MOI letter is therefore open, so 'only' and 'no waiver for a Pakistani degree' cannot be shown as Verified. A human could email the CS department and then record what they say.

Wrong program scope. The source is TUM's central language page, not the Informatics page. I re-read it live: the sentence just before the 'Verification of English Skills by Language of Instruction' section says alternative proofs depend on 'the Academic and Examination Regulations of your degree program (FPSO)' and on a 'Collective Amendment concerning the proof of English language proficiency'. That amendment link (portal.mytum.de/.../2018-02-SammelAeS-Sprachnachweis-FINAL-7-2-18.pdf/download) is dead: the MyTUM portal has been shut down and serves a notice page. The M.Sc. Informatics page (cit.tum.de, re-read live) asks only for 'Proof of your English language proficiency' and does not name the medium-of-instruction route (it requires a GRE from Pakistani applicants). ETH warns that a wrong language confirmation means direct rejection, since a certificate cannot be added after the deadline. Showing the 50% MOI rule as Verified for this program without the Informatics FPSO is too risky. A human should check the current FPSO for M.Sc. Informatics or ask CIT admissions.
